paper_title: Earth as a transducer for axion dark-matter detection
notes: Paper (arXiv:2112.09620, Arza et al.) presents new 95%-credible upper limits on the axion-photon coupling g_agamma from a search for an axion-DM-induced global magnetic field signal in SuperMAG magnetometer data, over 2e-18 eV < m_a < 7e-17 eV, assuming axion is all of DM with rho_dm = 0.3 GeV/cm^3. Text explicitly states the strongest smoothed limit g_agamma < 6.5e-11 GeV^-1 for 3e-17 eV < m_a < 4e-17 eV (comparable to CAST). Points outside this range are approximate values read from the described trend of Fig. 1 (limit weakens toward lower masses due to higher noise at lower frequencies); no numerical table is provided, so intermediate points carry ~factor-2 uncertainty. Limits include a 25% degradation factor for finite signal linewidth and account for stochastic axion amplitude fluctuations (Bayesian analysis). | selector: text (sole candidate) | axis-peek for confusable-family text read (#625 Phase 3c)
